PullRequest.Title: test(agentHost): cover legacy SDK v1 canvas extensions in the bundled runtime
PullRequest.Body:

Stacked on #349322 (SDK 2.0.1 bump); merge that first.

## Why

Published v1 canvas extensions (Kusto, session timeline) import `@github/copilot-sdk/extension` and pass a flat `canvases: [...]` array to `joinSession`. SDK 2.0.0 dropped both, so they crashed or lost their canvases. Nothing in our tests covered the legacy shape, so the regression shipped unnoticed.

## What changed

- `createCanvasContract` in `copilotSdkCanvas.integrationTest.ts` takes a `legacy` option that writes the provider like a v1 extension: legacy import and flat `canvases`. Existing variants are unchanged.
- New test opens a canvas from an eager legacy extension and from a lazy one whose `extension.json` declaration must still match what it registers, through the bundled extension SDK resolver and bootstrap (not a separately installed SDK).

## Scope

Flat `canvases` only: every installed v1 extension we found uses that and no flat hooks, tools or commands, and none use CommonJS `require`.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSdkCanvas.integrationTest.ts` with SDK 2.0.1: 6 passing (the 4 existing canvas tests plus the new one).
- Same file, `--grep legacy`, with main's SDK 2.0.0 installed: fails with `Test provider must register its canvas`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the new eager legacy canvas integration variant
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve bundled assets, write the isolated provider, start the runtime, create a session and register the eager provider, open its single canvas, observe readiness, then disconnect, stop and remove the temporary directory. This is integration-suite work, not application startup work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the SDK symlink, check bundled assets, create the temporary extension tree, write its module and remove the tree after use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One realpath lookup and five concurrent access checks per candidate package; candidates are bounded by two scope directories and at most two Linux platform variants. One temporary root, one recursive mkdir, one module write and one recursive cleanup for the eager variant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This additional variant did not exist. Existing integration variants already used the same bounded fixture and asset-resolution implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asset resolution and fixture writes precede client startup; cleanup precedes the lazy variant.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start a spawned-stdio runtime and launch the extension through the bundled bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime and one eager extension provider for the variant, followed by awaited session disconnect and client stop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No eager legacy test run; existing modern tests already exercised the same launch topology.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime and provider readiness precede successful canvas opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the session, list registered canvases, open one canvas, list open canvases, inspect extension status and disconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open and one extension-status list; each readiness helper makes at most 300 serial attempts, separated by 100 ms after failures, and exits immediately on success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No calls from this new variant; the polling helpers and their retry policy already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Readiness polling and the open RPC are awaited by the test. The returned localhost URL is parsed, not fetched.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One extension and one canvas in this variant; the entire new test has exactly two variants.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The eager and lazy variants run sequentially with cleanup awaited between them. Each variant creates one runtime client and one provider. Polling RPCs are sequential, not a concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each variant uses a fresh temporary HOME and runtime, so runtime/session state is cold. Asset resolution has no application cache; filesystem caches may be warm in the second variant. Polling stops at the first successful result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in fixed cardinality, sequential execution, bounded polling and explicit cleanup from the complete test and helper implementations. No independently problematic performance mechanism is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime startup duration is not measured, but this is intentional bounded integration coverage rather than newly scheduled production work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional test performs expected, constant-sized fixture and runtime work with cleanup; helper changes preserve the generated modern provider shape when legacy is false.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the canvas from the new lazy legacy integration variant
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After eager-variant cleanup, resolve assets and write the module plus declaration, start a fresh runtime and create a session, discover the declared canvas, then activate its provider on the first canvas.open call. Observe the open canvas and extension status before cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve assets and write extension.json plus extension.mjs; the generated provider imports its local declaration; finally remove the isolated root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same bounded asset checks as the eager variant, plus two fixture file writes rather than one. The declaration contains exactly one definition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The lazy modern fixture path already existed; this PR adds one use with a legacy import and flat canvases array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixture writes and discovery precede the open request; provider module/declaration loading occurs during first activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start one runtime and activate one extension provider through the bundled bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime and one provider for this variant; no runtime overlaps the eager variant by test control flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No lazy legacy test run. Existing lazy modern tests already exercised first-use provider activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider activation cost is on the first canvas-open path, as intended for lazy providers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover the canvas, open it with one small label input, observe readiness and inspect provider status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One canvas.open and one extensions.list; canvas.list and canvas.listOpen each stop on success or after 300 sequential attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These extra calls did not occur because this variant was absent; the existing helpers already bounded polling identically.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First open awaits provider activation. No HTTP request is made to the returned URL by the test.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sidecar declaration containing one canvas, one lazy extension, one open request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: This variant starts only after the eager variant has stopped and removed its root. Requests and readiness retries are awaited serially; no collection-wide process fan-out is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh isolated runtime state; declaration discovery represents a dormant provider, and first use activates it. No repeated opens, unbounded cache keys or failure-cache changes are introduced by this test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added work is one sequential cold fixture run and one first-use provider activation. SDK-internal activation details are external to the supplied source diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider startup latency and CI duration are unknown; neither changes the fixed input size or demonstrates a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Legacy generation changes the import and registration shape without adding definition multiplicity, retained state or repeated activation in repository code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the updated bundled Copilot SDK/runtime in local or remote Agent Host sessions and existing modern canvas lifecycle coverage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold production client resolves bundled assets alongside other startup assets, spawns the runtime and awaits client.start before sessions can proceed. Extension bootstrap launch remains on provider activation. Existing canvas tests continue to exercise open, reload and resume using the same modern generated definitions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Locate the platform runtime, native module, SDK and extension bootstrap assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One realpath plus five access checks per attempted candidate package, with at most four candidates on Linux and two elsewhere; unchanged by the version bump.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical resolver, candidate cardinality and startup placement with SDK 2.0.0/runtime 1.0.113.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required on cold client startup, shared with Browser Use through the existing runtimePaths promise; absent on cached ordinary-client acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the configured bundled runtime over stdio and launch activated extensions using the bundled bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime per effective cold client startup, with ordinary concurrent callers coalesced; extension launches remain activation-driven. A project extension launch also performs the existing module realpath check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host launch options, resolver and startup coalescing were used; the selected SDK changes from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1 and runtime metadata from 1.0.113 to 1.0.114.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime startup precedes client availability; extension activation precedes operations requiring that provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the SDK runtime connection for startup, session and canvas operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No repository call sites, loops, serialized payload sizes or request scheduling are changed outside the two new constant-sized test variants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stdio connection configuration and modern canvas registration shape were used before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing startup and requested session/canvas operations remain awaited in the same places.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Client startup attempts and activated extensions, not individual canvas metadata fields. The manifest/lockfile update keeps one pinned SDK version in each root/remote dependency graph and the same platform-specific optional package set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The ordinary production client reuses _client and coalesces in-flight startup through _clientStarting and _ensureClientHealing. Asset checks are five-way concurrent within a candidate and candidate packages are examined sequentially. Scoped clients remain separately owned; the diff changes none of these controls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm ordinary-client acquisition returns the existing client without resolving or spawning again. Cold asset resolution still uses realpath and access checks without introducing a cache. Modern fixture generation retains canvases.definitions; only explicitly legacy fixtures use a flat array.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that repository-level scheduling, host boundary cardinality and cleanup are unchanged. The external SDK/native-runtime implementation delta is not available in the supplied diff, so its internal CPU, allocation, network and persistence behavior cannot be established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements or dependency implementation comparison are available; a patch-version update alone does not establish a performance regression or performance-regression fix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression or qualifying regression-fix signal. Dependency internals are a meaningful review limitation, not evidence for a finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all five changed files and every diff page against base a96ff905be18b2322c7008945bd5242b9f9ac7f6. Traced fixture generation, bounded polling, sequential variant execution, cleanup, runtime asset resolution and production client coalescing. No actionable diff-introduced performance regressions found. Compatibility coverage is not evidence of a performance fix. External SDK/runtime implementation changes are not present in the supplied diff.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
